sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the coverage screen
sections.what: Brings in the state and data tools, the page link helper, the loading spinner and the request helper. It does not show anything on screen.
sections.why: These are needed to load data, keep the filter state, and move to project pages.

sections.name: SlideRef
sections.title: Slide reference shape
sections.what: Describes a slide reference: its number, id, kind and title.
sections.why: Lets each item point to the slides that show it.

sections.name: Item
sections.title: Coverage item shape
sections.what: Describes one item in the ledger, such as a project, fact, finding or source, with its project, pillar, placement reason, admission status, reason it was held, slides and source details.
sections.why: Gives the table one consistent set of fields to show.
sections.watch_out: Many fields can be empty, so the table must show blank or dash values instead of failing.

sections.name: Coverage, KIND_LABEL
sections.title: Coverage summary shape and item labels
sections.what: Describes the whole coverage result: totals per kind, per pillar and per placement reason. Also gives readable labels for each item kind, such as Projects and Facts.
sections.why: Lets the summary tables and headings show plain names instead of codes.
sections.watch_out: An item kind missing from the labels will show its raw code.

sections.name: BASIS_LABEL, slideText
sections.title: Placement reason labels and slide text
sections.what: Gives readable names for each placement reason, such as keyword match or held back. Also turns a list of slides into short references like S3.
sections.why: Explains to readers why an item went where it did, without showing internal codes.
sections.watch_out: A new placement reason from the server will show its raw code until it is added here.

sections.name: CoverageView (part 1)
sections.title: Loading data and the summary tables
sections.what: Loads the summary for the run and the list for the chosen kind. Filters the list by project name, excerpt or publisher text. Shows a spinner while loading, a message if no ledger exists, the summary table with counts that can be clicked to change the kind, and the placement reason and pillar breakdown.
sections.why: Gives an overview first, then lets the user drill into one kind of item.
sections.watch_out: Any error from the summary request is treated as a missing ledger, so a server outage looks the same as an absent record.

sections.name: CoverageView (part 2)
sections.title: Filtered item table and row limit
sections.what: Shows the filter box, a table with the project or source, outcome or excerpt, pillar, placement reason, held reason and slides. It shows at most 600 rows and says how many were left out. Project names link to the project page, and sources link to their web address.
sections.why: Lets users check individual items and open the project behind them. The row limit keeps the page responsive.
sections.watch_out: The 600 row limit means some items are hidden until the filter narrows the list, so a total count can seem higher than what is visible.

summary: This file shows the coverage ledger for a run, which lists every fact, finding and source the run collected and where each one was placed in the deck.
purpose: Lets users check what the run used, what it held back, and which slides show each item, so they can judge the completeness of the lessons.
why: The file header says it shows the same ledger that appears on the project side. Reason for the separate view is not stated in the code.
how: It defines the shapes for coverage items and summaries. It loads a summary for the run, then loads a list for the chosen kind of item. The user can switch kind by clicking a summary row and filter the list by text. The list shows up to 600 rows, with links to projects or sources and slide numbers.
inputs: The run id, the kind chosen by the user, and the text in the filter box.
outputs: Summary tables, a breakdown by placement reason and pillar, and a filtered table of items with links and slide references.
risks: Only the first 600 rows are shown, so a filter must be used to see the rest. If the coverage request fails, the screen shows a message that no ledger is recorded, which can hide a server problem.
debug: If the view says no ledger exists, check that the run produced coverage data and that the coverage request returns. If rows look wrong, compare the item kind and the filter text. If a project link fails, check the project id.
